title: The manifest writer claims legacy jobs remain automatically recoverable even though the trust gate and tests deliberately reject them
observed_behavior: The writer comment says legacy manifests remain writable so existing parked jobs can still be recovered and drained. The same module rejects missing schema_version as LEGACY_MANIFEST and every non-v1 schema as SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH before repair or drain, while the safety suite explicitly requires a legacy_manifest.v0 fixture to recover zero outputs and leave the payload parked.
expected_invariant: Compatibility comments at a release-critical recovery boundary must distinguish legacy inventory visibility and manual recovery from automatic repair/drain eligibility, and must agree with the executable trust policy and its tests.
root_cause: The writer retained an older backward-compatibility explanation after the pending-manifest trust boundary was strengthened to fail closed on every legacy or non-current schema.
failure_scenario: A maintainer relies on the inline contract while changing legacy recovery, preserves permissive writes believing automatic drain is supported, or documents an upgrade path that does not exist. Operators with legacy parked jobs then expect recovery that the engine intentionally refuses, increasing diagnosis time at an already exceptional recovery boundary.
evidence: pending_manifest_store.ps1 lines 319-324 returns LEGACY_MANIFEST or SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH before repair/drain trust succeeds.
pending_manifest_store.ps1 lines 803-805 and 873-880 still permit a legacy writer round trip and state that legacy jobs can be recovered and drained.
Invoke-PendingPublishSafetyChecks.ps1 lines 556-580 creates legacy_manifest.v0 and asserts drained=0, payload retained, and no final output.
The independent reviewer read all 924 current source lines and reproduced the current trust decisions with no-write probes.
affected_flows: operator expectations for legacy parked jobs
future edits to manifest round-trip validation and trust policy
existing_safeguards: Runtime trust fails closed and preserves the parked payload.
The safety suite explicitly verifies that a legacy manifest does not publish.
Backend inventory keeps legacy rows visible for operator diagnosis.
safeguard_gap: Executable behavior is safe, but the nearest maintenance explanation describes the opposite compatibility outcome and no nearby text identifies legacy recovery as manual-only.
tests_present: ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-PendingPublishSafetyChecks.ps1 asserts legacy schema rejection and non-mutation.
Python pending-publish service tests retain legacy inventory visibility.
tests_missing: A source/doc consistency assertion is not appropriate; the missing control is an accurate inline explanation and an explicit, tested migration workflow if automatic legacy recovery is desired.
recommended_remediation: Rewrite the writer comment to say legacy manifests may round-trip for inventory/manual evidence but are not eligible for automatic repair or drain. If product requirements call for migration, implement an explicit backend-owned, hash-binding upgrade flow with preview/confirmation and tests rather than weakening the trust gate.
remediation_risk: Low for correcting the comment. High if automatic migration is added, because legacy records lack the current transaction, identity, and byte-proof guarantees.
validation_rung: Comment-only correction requires focused path/reference checks and change-packet validation; any migration implementation requires pending safety, fault-injection, repair/drain integration, and representative payload validation.
prior_audit_relationship: No current finding recorded this exact contradiction between the writer compatibility comment and the deliberate legacy trust rejection.
